evidence: The owner pushes EAX at 0x009f8e and reaches the sole matching POP EAX/RET at 0x00a0c0/0x00a0c2. The now-recovered 0x00a2ab CFG can reach a CALL at 0x00a2d9, but that edge supplies no matching four-byte stack value and cannot return correctly through the POP EAX epilogue; retain it as a reviewed dead/error edge rather than a function boundary.

Entry 0x0270 falls through 0x0477 after computing EAX from the parent Y transform; 0x0477 immediately stores that live EAX, later decrements the shared state count, jumps back to 0x0279, and reaches the only RET at 0x0548. No call or independent live-in contract exists at 0x0477, so it is an internal label in the matrix/tree-transform routine.

The face loop at 0x0700 reaches 0x0775 by physical fallthrough after its final LOOP, with geometry DS, raster ES, and active-data FS still live. No call targets 0x0775; its pool initialization, bucket scan, face activation, span construction, framebuffer fill, and column advance all return through 0x0848 as part of the 0x0700 renderer.

Offset 0x0848 is the sole near RET shared by the 0x0700 renderer's empty-table and completed-column paths and by 0x0D7D's empty-free-list rejection. It has no call entry or independent body, so the one-byte label is an internal shared epilogue rather than an empty function.

Offset 0x0849 is reached only by the 0x0898 back edge while the 0x0700 renderer insertion-sorts active raster records after advancing a column. Its live SI/DI records and linked-list continuation at 0x0884 come from the owner; no call targets it.

Offset 0x0C2A is the inner-loop head reached by physical fallthrough from texture setup at 0x0C27 and by its own 0x0C3D back edge. It consumes live texture, framebuffer, interpolation, and row-count state and eventually rejoins the 0x0C91 owner continuation; no call targets it.

Entry 0x0D7D loads the face's three vertex offsets and the active raster record, jumps to the shared 0x0848 RET only when no record is available, and otherwise falls directly through 0x0D93 with BX, DI, BP, and SI live. No call targets 0x0D93, and every gradient exit returns from the 0x0D7D call, so 0x0D93 is an internal continuation rather than a function boundary.
